title: Bounded exact-term Hom preserves quasi-isomorphisms with independent site universes
statement: Let $J$ be a Grothendieck topology on a small category $C$, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $P$ a cochain complex of sheaves of $R$-modules. Suppose $P^n=0$ outside a finite interval and that each functor $\mathcal Hom_R(P^n,-)$ sends short exact sequences to short exact sequences. For every quasi-isomorphism $f:M\to N$ of arbitrary cochain complexes [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], the induced map $\mathcal Hom^\bullet_R(P,M)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet_R(P,N)$ [def-pur-hom-complex] is a quasi-isomorphism. Here the site has object universe c and morphism universe v, the commutative coefficient ring and module sheaves have universe max c v r, and the sheafification hypotheses are explicit. No equality of these universes is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08DM (cohomology-lemma-RHom-strictly-perfect), bounded Hom calculation; homology.tex Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain) for finite-filtration induction

proof.text: Induct on a natural interval width d with P supported in [a,a+d]. For d=0 apply the single-degree Hom theorem at a. Internal Hom from zero is zero, so all-zero sources are included.

For a successor width, form the real Mathlib stupid tail U in degrees at least a+1. It is supported in [a+1,a+1+d]. Its terms are either zero or isomorphic to the corresponding P terms. Prove exactness for zero sources and transport short exactness along those isomorphisms. Apply the induction hypothesis to U. Apply the single-degree theorem to P^a placed in degree a, transporting the exact-term hypothesis along singleObjXSelf.

Use the natural short exact Hom sequences for the stupid tail. Transport the two outer quasi-isomorphisms through their arrow isomorphisms. Apply the proved upstream HomologicalComplex.HomologySequence.quasiIso_τ₂ (WeilConjectures.FromJoel.Algebra.Homology.BicomplexColumns), whose long-exact-sequence proof uses the five lemma. Transport the middle quasi-isomorphism back through its arrow isomorphism.
For the original bounds a,b take d=(b-a).toNat. Then b is at most a+d, including b<a; the given bounds imply the interval hypothesis. Apply the proved finite induction.

proof_origin.place: Bounded exact-term argument; Lean finite-width induction by P3, using the upstream long-exact-sequence quasiIso_τ₂ lemma after independent second reading

theorem quasiIso_homComplex_map_of_bounded_exact_termsOfUniverses
    {C : Type c} [Category.{v} C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max c v r}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max c v r}]
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max c v r})
    (P : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{max c v r}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max c v r} RingCat.{max c v r})).obj R)) ℤ)
    (hbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (P.X n))
    (hexact : ∀ (n : ℤ) (S : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{max c v r}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max c v r} RingCat.{max c v r})).obj R))),
      S.ShortExact → ∃ hz : SheafOfModules.homObjMap.{max c v r, v, c, max c v r} (R := R) (𝟙 (P.X
          n)) S.f ≫
          SheafOfModules.homObjMap.{max c v r, v, c, max c v r} (R := R) (𝟙 (P.X n)) S.g = 0,
        (ShortComplex.mk (SheafOfModules.homObjMap.{max c v r, v, c, max c v r} (R := R) (𝟙 (P.X
            n)) S.f)
          (SheafOfModules.homObjMap.{max c v r, v, c, max c v r} (R := R) (𝟙 (P.X n)) S.g)
              hz).ShortExact)
    {M N : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{max c v r}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max c v r} RingCat.{max c v r})).obj R)) ℤ}
    (f : M ⟶ N) [QuasiIso f] :
    QuasiIso (((homComplexFunctor.{c, v, max c v r, max c v r} (R := R)).obj (op P)).map f)
